# Eric Lombardi

> Eric Lombardi is a Toronto-based strategy consultant in financial services and technology, a writer on Ontario's economy and growth, founder of More Neighbours Toronto, and the 2026 Ontario Liberal leadership candidate who published a fully costed platform for the province.

Email: eric@ericlombardi.ca. Location: Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Socials: LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/in/ericlombardi, X https://x.com/EricDLombardi, Bluesky https://bsky.app/profile/ericlombardi.ca, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/ericlombardi, YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@EricDLombardi

## Public policy work

- [Ontario Liberal leadership, 2026](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/policy/ontario-liberal-leadership-2026/): Candidate for Leader. A province-wide leadership campaign built on economic growth and government capability, with the race's first fully costed platform: thirteen policy areas and more than 190 commitments.
- [More Neighbours Toronto](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/policy/more-neighbours-toronto/): Founder and president. Canada's largest grassroots housing-abundance organization: a non-partisan network of pro-housing voices that turns up to say yes to more homes, in every neighbourhood.
- [Build Toronto](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/policy/build-toronto/): Chair and co-founder. The Toronto chapter of Build Canada: founders, operators and civic leaders publishing concrete, ambitious proposals for the city on housing, infrastructure, governance and growth.

## Writing (own site)

- [What My Policy Survey Says About Ontario Right Now](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/what-my-policy-survey-says-about-ontario-right-now/) (2026-05-28, Campaign notes): People are frustrated by the status quo, worried about affordability, and impatient with institutional failure.
- [Alto should be just the beginning of Ontario's high-speed rail network](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/alto-should-be-just-the-beginning/) (2026-04-29, Infrastructure and transit): And I built a tool to show what this could mean.
- [An Ontario Budget For Decline & War In Iran](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/an-ontario-budget-for-decline-war-in-iran/) (2026-03-23, Economy and growth): Ontario's budget arrives this week. Before it does, it's worth being clear about the province it lands in…
- [A Billion Here, A Billion There](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/a-billion-here-a-billion-there/) (2026-03-08, Economy and growth): What creates the most value for Ontarians? Plus, what we can do about shootings targeting Jewish-Canadians, and learnings on tax competitiveness.
- [“Poorer Than Alabama?” — What the GDP Per Capita Debate Is Really About](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/poorer-than-alabama-gdp-per-capita-debate/) (2026-02-27, Economy and growth): Regardless of metric, Canada, and specifically Ontario, is not growing as fast as we should.
- [Hamilton Speech, University Funding Changes, And Other Thoughts](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/hamilton-speech-university-funding-changes-and-other-thoughts/) (2026-02-17, Campaign notes): An idea for Ontario's university funding, thoughts on Canada's fertility crisis, and what it means to truly build a province where young people can thrive.
- [Liberal Leadership Timelines are Out](https://elombardi-website.github.io/ericlombardi-site/writing/liberal-leadership-timelines-are-out/) (2026-02-07, Campaign notes): Thoughts on the new election rules, and why my visit to the long-delayed Eglinton LRT only deepened my commitment to fixing Ontario's infrastructure cost problem.
